question: Can training against a stronger post-trained teacher improve a standalone two-pass Base-derived decoder without truncating the Base thinking budget or losing raw language quality?
training: Keep every original dense Base parameter fixed. Copy each 8-rank parent factor (compensating the deployment scale) and its gate. Add at most 24 new singular directions per linear projection from the frozen official post-trained sibling-minus-Base weight update, initialized at 0.85 scale by two randomized native MLX range refinements. Add no embedding, norm, dense donor or output head. Record retained energy per matrix. Then use 96 native AdamW updates on independently sampled math, real reading and prose. Greedily sample up to 48 training-only teacher solutions at 640 tokens and require at least 10 complete correct traces, targeting 20. Use every selected trace twice. For every supervised example distill the top 32 probabilities plus residual mass at 24 positions, in addition to CE on all response IDs. Each update includes a plain-text anchor distilled from ordinary pinned Base. A single trained K2 model performs all inference without donor, reranking or special-cased prompt routing.
decision: Direct native 48-item pair, identical thinking prompt IDs, greedy first-turn and common 1024-token cap. Require pooled net >=4 and positive per source, total elapsed <=Base, no negative source at the 256 prefix, and 9328-target ungated V3 loss <=Base +0.03. Additionally audit every completed strict-invalid answer on both arms for mathematical content. Report teacher access and unknown pretraining overlap. A failure closes confirmation of this checkpoint. A pass permits a fresh publisher-test and SVAMP replication and a matched trained dense attribution control. Stop on prefix-data yield, budget or memory guard.
